element: Proficiency level definitions (Foundational 0-2y / Intermediate 3-5 / Advanced 6-10 / Expert 10+)
rationale: Tenure bands cannot be used in federal qualification or assessment: quals are based on specialized experience equivalent to the next lower grade, and OPM states degrees/tenure are poor proxies. Redefine levels by independence, complexity and scope (parallel to FES Factors 2, 4, 5) and publish an indicative grade-band map (see report)

element: Advanced/Expert knowledge statements ('Expert in...', 'Shapes...')
rationale: Not usable as SME-QA benchmarks or structured-interview anchors; they restate the level name. Rewrite as observable work outcomes at the level

element: Expert-level indicators
rationale: Reputation and publication are not job-related behaviors for most federal positions and would fail a job-relatedness review if used in rating; keep research outputs only for research-grade (RGEG) roles

element: Intermediate-level indicators
rationale: Largely behavioral and close to what SMEs write in crediting plans (e.g., 'Determines appropriate level of NEPA analysis'); best v1 raw material for job analysis

element: Job tasks T1-T3 per competency
rationale: Usable seed for task inventories but too few and too coarse; job analysis needs 15-40 position-specific tasks rated for importance/frequency/needed-at-entry. Add frequency/importance placeholders and allow many-to-many task-competency links

element: Labor Market Crosswalk (family -> SOC only)
rationale: Add family->OPM series and competency->series crosswalks (this folder's register and crosswalk). Several SOC targets are wrong (see next rows)

element: F12 Fire Management -> 33-1021 'Fire Inspectors'
rationale: 33-1021 is First-Line Supervisors of Firefighting and Prevention Workers; primary should be 33-2011 Firefighters with 33-2022 Forest Fire Inspectors and Prevention Specialists and 33-1021 as secondaries. Federal home is OPM 0456/0462

element: F13 Env Health & Justice -> 29-9021 'Health Information Technologists'
rationale: 29-9021 (Health Information Technologists and Medical Registrars) is not environmental health. Use 19-2041 Environmental Scientists and Specialists, Including Health; 19-5011 Occupational Health and Safety Specialists; 19-4042 technicians

element: F11 Env Education -> 25-2031 / 25-4031 'Library Technicians'
rationale: 25-4031 is wrong; federal interpreters/educators map to OPM 0025/1701 and SOC 19-1031 (park naturalists sit there in O*NET) or 25-9031 Instructional Coordinators; verify with O*NET-SOC 2019

element: F10 Sustainable Agriculture -> 19-1012 labelled 'Farm & Home Mgmt Educators'
rationale: Code/title mismatch: 19-1012 is Food Scientists and Technologists; Farm and Home Management Educators is 25-9021. Better primary: 19-1013 Soil and Plant Scientists; federal home 0457/0470/0471

element: Missing SOC 19-2041 Environmental Scientists and Specialists, Including Health
rationale: Largest environmental SOC detailed occupation is absent; it is the natural crosswalk for OPM 0028 and much of 0401

element: Sector application note 'Public Agencies'
rationale: Lumps federal, state, local and Tribal governments whose authorities, hiring systems and statecraft differ; split into federal/state/local/Tribal enactment notes (SL, TN lanes)

element: Profession families as federal role proxies (F1-F15 Core/Supporting)
rationale: Series-level core sets agree poorly with family Core: e.g., 0454 2/7, 0462 2/7, 1315 2/8 core competencies are family-Core. Federal positions carry permit, contract, NEPA and enforcement duties families omit. Keep families as identity views; build role profiles keyed to series x grade band

element: F1 Forestry Core set
rationale: Omits 3.1.4 (timber sale/stewardship contract administration) and 6.1.4 (NEPA), both grade-relevant duties for federal 0460s

element: F4 Water Resources Core set
rationale: FC-heavy; federal 1315 hydrologist core is DC-heavy (7/8 core competencies DC primary): modeling, time series, sensor networks, data review

element: General competencies mixed into technical domains (5.1.1, 5.1.2, 3.3.1, 3.5.x, 2.5.x)
rationale: Crosswalk to OPM general competency names (Writing, Oral Communication, Teamwork, Decision Making, Leadership/ECQs) rather than defining parallel versions; USA Hire already measures general competencies by series and grade

element: 3.4.3 Cryptocurrency, digital payments and decentralized finance
rationale: No federal environmental position performs this; not an assessable requirement for any OPM series in the register

element: 5.3.4 Diversity, equity and inclusion practices
rationale: Federal DEIA programs and related guidance were rescinded in 2025 (OPM notes rescission of DEI guidance on its memo index); a federal role profile cannot list this as a requirement. State/NGO use differs (SL). CA to decide reframing (e.g., accessibility, inclusive public engagement)

element: 6.7.2 Environmental justice screening and assessment
rationale: Federal EJ program direction changed in 2025 (SC lane to verify); keep for state/local/NGO profiles; mark federal enactment as variable

element: 6.1.4 NEPA process implementation
rationale: Indicators reference CEQ regulations; NEPA procedures changed in 2025 (SC to verify). Rewrite tool/regulation-neutral and attach regulation versions in the tools/standards layer

element: Reform-sensitivity flags (6 codes)
rationale: Useful idea; represent as dated policy events (L5) so HR users can see which duties a rule change touched; add MHP/CTCA, Schedule P/C, series consolidation and RIF-rule events

element: Task 13 exposure tags (auto type, career ladder P/C/X, CLD)
rationale: Valuable for workforce planning (use case d) when labelled single-analyst judgment; derived signal: 86% of entry (P) tasks under 0028 core competencies are Ac/S/V vs 12% for 0456

element: opm_taxonomy_crossdomain_analysis: claim 'No Environmental Data Science series'
rationale: Data Science series 1560 exists (established 2021 [J]); OPM also issued AI competency models (2024) and a competency-based 2210 standard (2026)

element: opm_taxonomy_crossdomain_analysis: 'Only 1370 explicitly mentions GIS'; datacraft 'WEAK across all series'
rationale: Method error: classification standards are deliberately tool-agnostic; datacraft recognition must be read from PDs, postings, qualification selective factors and OPM interpretive guidance. Conclusion overstated; 0150, 1560, 0401 GIS specialists exist

element: opm_taxonomy_crossdomain_analysis: quoted 'OPM language' per series
rationale: Quotes are uncited and several read like paraphrase (e.g., HAZMAT response for 0028); re-extract verbatim from standards with page cites before any external use

element: opm_taxonomy_crossdomain_analysis: '0401 Fire - General Bio Sciences Fire Specialty' row
rationale: Wildland fire management work now has its own series 0456 (2022 [J])

element: opm_taxonomy_crossdomain_analysis: 'Environmental policy professionals classified as 0343 or 0301'
rationale: Incomplete: also 0028, 0101, 0110, 0401 and 0905 attorneys; senior policy roles now partly Schedule Policy/Career

element: opm_taxonomy_crossdomain_analysis: 'Interdisciplinary positions mentioned but rare in practice'
rationale: Contrary to professional experience: interdisciplinary PDs (e.g., 0401/0408/0486) are common for land-agency professional positions [J]; needs PD sample to settle

element: opm_taxonomy_crossdomain_analysis: '0400 JFS last revised 2005'
rationale: Not verified this session; OPM Phase One consolidation (2026) and planned redesign make the standard date less important than the realignment schedule

element: opm_taxonomy_crossdomain_analysis: '292-competency taxonomy'
rationale: Outdated count (v1 has 222)

element: opm_taxonomy_crossdomain_analysis: Fieldcraft strongly recognized in 0400 and 0025 series
rationale: Consistent with series definitions and the crosswalk (FC dominates 0456, 0457, 0462, 0486 core sets)

element: forester_pd_transformation: PD format (Major Duties + 'Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities' list)
rationale: Federal FES PDs use major duties with % time plus Factors 1-9; KSA lists are a vacancy-announcement artifact. Rebuild the redesigned PD in FES format with Factor 1 knowledge statements drawn from EMST

element: forester_pd_transformation: duty time shifts (inventory 25% -> ~12%; sale admin 20% -> ~12%)
rationale: Speculative; and it omits the classification consequence - if grade-controlling duties shrink below the regular-and-recurring/25% threshold the grade or series can change. Any 'redesigned PD' must go through a classifier

element: forester_pd_transformation: 'Functional positions' (Sensing...Deciding) as the PD organizing structure
rationale: Not a classifiable PD structure; keep functional positions as an analytic lens on top of major duties

element: forester_pd_transformation: striking 'skill in GIS' and 'cruising' KSAs
rationale: Reword rather than strike: the requirement shifts from performing to verifying; field measurement remains a qualification for entry

element: forester_pd_transformation: career-ladder disruption via cruising
rationale: Keep hypothesis but relocate: much cruising/marking is done by 0462 technicians and seasonals; the entry path at risk is 0462/0499 -> 0460, now compounded by 2025 contraction of student-trainee occupations and under-30 share (7.9%)

element: forester_pd_transformation: four new competencies (remote sensing calibration; AI growth model evaluation; climate-adaptive silviculture; developmental pathway mentorship)
rationale: Carried as candidate competencies FH-C05/FH-C06 and mapped to 1.7.2/7.2.1; label J until PD/posting sample confirms

element: Missing federal fields: OPM series code, grade band, positive-education flag, duty-statement templates, Factor 1 knowledge statements, needed-at-entry flag
rationale: Required for every HR use case in hr_use_cases.md
